/plants/anacacho-orchid-tree.name: Anacacho Orchid Tree
/plants/anacacho-orchid-tree.description: Features leaves shaped like butterflies. Good as a small patio tree. May be sold as B. congesta.

/plants/angelita-daisy.name: Angelita Daisy
/plants/angelita-daisy.description: Colorful and persistent, good for small spaces and narrow areas. Previously classified as Hymenoxys acaulis.

/plants/argentine-giant.name: Argentine Giant
/plants/argentine-giant.description: Boasts fragrant, striking flowers that are 6 to 8 inches across. Also try E. oxygona. Previously classified as Trichocereus candicans.

/plants/argentine-hedgehog.name: Argentine Hedgehog
/plants/argentine-hedgehog.description: Features some of the most spectacular flowers of all landscape cacti. Look for selections that offer a wide range of flower colors. Previously classified as Trichocereus huascha.

/plants/arizona-poppy.name: Arizona Poppy
/plants/arizona-poppy.description: Summer bloomer. Sow seeds in the spring. Germinates with summer rains.

/plants/arizona-rosewood.name: Arizona Rosewood
/plants/arizona-rosewood.description: Can be grown as a small tree. Native alternative to oleander.

/plants/arizona-yellow-bells.name: Arizona Yellow Bells
/plants/arizona-yellow-bells.description: Provides summer color with yellow, trumpet-like flowers that attract hummingbirds. Look for selections that offer larger flower and leaf sizes. Also try T. stans v. stans.

/plants/arroyo-lupine.name: Arroyo Lupine
/plants/arroyo-lupine.description: Sow seeds in the fall. Also try L. arizonicus, L. sparsiflorus.

/plants/autumn-sage.name: Autumn Sage
/plants/autumn-sage.description: Bright red flowers in spring and fall. Does best in low deserts if planted in partial sun.

/plants/baja-fairy-duster.name: Baja Fairy Duster
/plants/baja-fairy-duster.description: Can serve as a good informal hedge. May be sold as C. peninsularis.

/plants/baja-passion-vine.name: Baja Passion Vine
/plants/baja-passion-vine.description: Striking flowers. Attracts the Gulf Fritillary Butterfly.

/plants/baja-ruellia.name: Baja Ruellia
/plants/baja-ruellia.description: Tolerates some shade. Flowers attract hummingbirds. Also try R. californica.

/plants/bamboo-muhly.name: Bamboo Muhly
/plants/bamboo-muhly.description: Resembles short bamboo and does well in containers.

/plants/banana-yucca.name: Banana Yucca
/plants/banana-yucca.description: Can serve as an effective security plant or barrier. Features a striking show of flowers. Pollinated by yucca moths. Also try Y. aloifolia.

/plants/barberry.name: Barberry
/plants/barberry.description: Can serve as a good informal hedge. Red berries attract birds, foliage provides shelter. Also try B. haematocarpa. May be sold as Mahonia trifoliolata or Agarita.

/plants/beargrass.name: Beargrass
/plants/beargrass.description: Grass-like form softens hard elements in the landscape. Does well in containers.

/plants/beavertail-prickly-pear.name: Beavertail Prickly Pear
/plants/beavertail-prickly-pear.description: Bright magenta-pink blooms provide vibrant spring color.

/plants/bee-brush.name: Bee Brush
/plants/bee-brush.description: Scented flowers and fragrant foliage. May be sold as A. lycioides.

/plants/blackbrush-acacia.name: Blackbrush Acacia
/plants/blackbrush-acacia.description: Effective as a barrier. Boasts attractive light gray bark. Previously classified as Acacia rigidula.

/plants/blackfoot-daisy.name: Blackfoot Daisy
/plants/blackfoot-daisy.description: Plant this bright and colorful groundcover in well-drained soil.

/plants/blanket-flower.name: Blanket Flower
/plants/blanket-flower.description: Summer bloomer. Sow seeds in the fall to spring.

/plants/blue-flax.name: Blue Flax
/plants/blue-flax.description: Sow seeds in the fall. Reseeds readily. Does better with partial shade.

/plants/blue-grama.name: Blue Grama
/plants/blue-grama.description: Features unique seedheads that resemble eyelashes. Good for meadows.

/plants/blue-myrtle-cactus.name: Blue Myrtle Cactus
/plants/blue-myrtle-cactus.description: Can become tree-like with age. Purple fruits follow fragrant flowers.

/plants/blue-palo-verde.name: Blue Palo Verde
/plants/blue-palo-verde.description: Offers vivid spring color from a full canopy of yellow blooms. Provides seed and cover to birds and other wildlife. Previously classified as Cercidium floridum.

/plants/blue-yucca.name: Blue Yucca
/plants/blue-yucca.description: Striking bluish color makes it a great accent. Pollinated by yucca moths. Also try Y. rostrata.

/plants/bougainvillea.name: Bougainvillea
/plants/bougainvillea.description: Accepts hot exposures. Selections available in a wide range of flower colors, sizes, and forms - including shrubs. May be sold as B. brasiliensis.

/plants/brittlebush.name: Brittlebush
/plants/brittlebush.description: Good for naturalistic landscapes. Provides food and shelter for birds and small mammals.

/plants/buckhorn-cholla.name: Buckhorn Cholla
/plants/buckhorn-cholla.description: Provides excellent nesting habitat and wildlife shelter. Makes an effective security barrier. Also try C. imbricata, C. spinosior, and C. versicolor. May be sold as Opuntia acanthocarpa.

/plants/bush-dalea.name: Bush Dalea
/plants/bush-dalea.description: Provides winter color and attracts butterflies.

/plants/candelilla.name: Candelilla
/plants/candelilla.description: Features clusters of slender upright, leafless stems. Does well in containers. Sap may irritate skin. Also try E. resinifera.

/plants/canyon-hackberry.name: Canyon Hackberry
/plants/canyon-hackberry.description: Has a distinctive trunk. Birds relish its tiny orange berries. Provides food and shelter for wildlife.

/plants/canyon-penstemon.name: Canyon Penstemon
/plants/canyon-penstemon.description: Plant in the fall for spring flowers. Reseeds readily. Also try P. triflorus.

/plants/cape-aloe.name: Cape Aloe
/plants/cape-aloe.description: Showy candelabra-shaped flower spikes attract hummingbirds. Provides an \\

/plants/cape-honeysuckle.name: Cape Honeysuckle
/plants/cape-honeysuckle.description: With support, can be trained as a vine. Previously classified as Tecomaria capensis.

/plants/cardon-grande.name: Cardon Grande
/plants/cardon-grande.description: Somewhat similar in form to the saguaro but grows faster and is smaller at maturity. Previously classified as Trichocereus terscheckii.

/plants/cascalote.name: Cascalote
/plants/cascalote.description: Stunning, fragrant winter flowers are followed by colorful seed pods. Previously classified as Caesalpinia cacalaco.

/plants/catclaw-vine.name: Catclaw Vine
/plants/catclaw-vine.description: Provides fast cover but can damage walls and fences. Previously classified as Macfadyena unguis-cati.

/plants/chaparral-sage.name: Chaparral Sage
/plants/chaparral-sage.description: Highly fragrant foliage. May be short-lived.

/plants/chaste-tree.name: Chaste Tree
/plants/chaste-tree.description: Fragrant flowers. Seeds are hazardous on sidewalks. Look for selections that offer a variety of flower colors and sizes.

/plants/chihuahuan-sage.name: Chihuahuan Sage
/plants/chihuahuan-sage.description: Fragrant flowers in response to monsoon rains. Good as an informal hedge. Accepts poor soils.

/plants/chinese-pistache.name: Chinese Pistache
/plants/chinese-pistache.description: Dense shade tree that provides striking fall color. Red fruit on female trees. Look for 'Red Push' and other Pistacia selections. Allergenic (caused by male pollen).

/plants/chocolate-flower.name: Chocolate Flower
/plants/chocolate-flower.description: Fragrant flowers have a distinctive chocolate scent.

/plants/chuparosa.name: Chuparosa
/plants/chuparosa.description: Provides good winter color and can be used as an informal hedge. Look for selections with yellow flowers.

/plants/compass-barrel.name: Compass Barrel
/plants/compass-barrel.description: Good for naturalistic landscapes. May be sold as F. acanthodes. Also try F. herrerae and F. wislizeni.

/plants/coolibah.name: Coolibah
/plants/coolibah.description: Large, fast growing, and accepts lawn conditions. Also try E. erythrocorys.

/plants/coral-penstemon.name: Coral Penstemon
/plants/coral-penstemon.description: Plant in the fall for spring flowers. Reseeds readily.

/plants/cows-horn-agave.name: Cow's Horn Agave
/plants/cows-horn-agave.description: Reddish brown marginal teeth are highly decorative.

/plants/creeping-germander.name: Creeping Germander
/plants/creeping-germander.description: Provides fragrant foliage. Requires well-drained soil.

/plants/creosote-bush.name: Creosote Bush
/plants/creosote-bush.description: Good for naturalistic landscapes and can serve as an informal screen. Distinctively fragrant foliage after rain. Provides food and shelter for wildlife. May be sold as L. divaricata.

/plants/damianita.name: Damianita
/plants/damianita.description: Fragrant foliage and a good groundcover for courtyards. Seeds are eaten by birds and small mammals.

/plants/deer-grass.name: Deer Grass
/plants/deer-grass.description: Versatile grass with lush foliage and interesting flowers. Also try M. emersleyi, M. lindheimeri, and M. rigida.

/plants/desert-bluebell.name: Desert Bluebells
/plants/desert-bluebell.description: Sow seeds in the fall or plant from containers. Plant parts can irritate skin. Also try P. tanacetifolia.

/plants/desert-hackberry.name: Desert Hackberry
/plants/desert-hackberry.description: Orange berries attract birds. Branches and leaves provide shelter for wildlife.

/plants/desert-lavender.name: Desert Lavender
/plants/desert-lavender.description: Fragrant foliage and tiny, lavender flowers that attract bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. May be sold as Condea emoryi.

/plants/desert-marigold.name: Desert Marigold
/plants/desert-marigold.description: Provides color for long periods of time and reseeds easily. Undemanding and low maintenance.

/plants/desert-milkweed.name: Desert Milkweed
/plants/desert-milkweed.description: Strong vertical accent and important butterfly host plant. Also try A. linaria.

/plants/desert-senna.name: Desert Senna
/plants/desert-senna.description: Bright yellow flowers that bloom spring to fall.

/plants/desert-spoon.name: Desert Spoon
/plants/desert-spoon.description: Distinct accent plant with twisting leaves. Stalk bloom attracts bees, butterflies, and other pollinators. Also try D. acrotriche for shady areas.

/plants/desert-willow.name: Desert Willow
/plants/desert-willow.description: Deciduous throughout the colder months, dropping its leaves in late fall. Beautiful trumpet-shaped flowers, occurring spring to fall, attract hummingbirds and are pollinated by carpenter bees and bumblebees. Look for selections that offer a variety of flower colors, branching structures, and leaf forms.

/plants/elephants-food.name: Elephant's Food
/plants/elephants-food.description: Adapted to many different conditions. Good in containers. Look for smaller cultivars, as some selections can reach 12 feet or taller.

/plants/engelmanns-hedgehog.name: Engelmann's Hedgehog
/plants/engelmanns-hedgehog.description: Vibrant magenta blooms provide intense spring color.

/plants/engelmanns-prickly-pear.name: Engelmann's Prickly Pear
/plants/engelmanns-prickly-pear.description: Large, dark red fruits attract birds and other wildlife.

/plants/evergreen-elm.name: Evergreen Elm
/plants/evergreen-elm.description: Features attractive bark and accepts lawn conditions.

/plants/feather-bush.name: Feather Bush
/plants/feather-bush.description: Lush appearance and can be grown as a shrub or into a small tree. May be sold as L. microphylla v. thornberi.

/plants/feathery-senna.name: Feathery Senna
/plants/feathery-senna.description: Provides good winter color. Fragrant flowers. May be sold as Cassia artemisioides. Also try S. artemisioides v. oligophylla, v. petiolaris, and v. sturtii.

/plants/firebush.name: Firebush
/plants/firebush.description: Provides colorful reddish foliage in winter and brilliant red flower blooms in summer.

/plants/firecracker-penstemon.name: Firecracker Penstemon
/plants/firecracker-penstemon.description: Plant in the fall for spring flowers. Reseeds readily.

/plants/five-spot.name: Five Spot
/plants/five-spot.description: Striking, unusual flowers. Sow seeds in the fall.

/plants/flame-honeysuckle.name: Flame Honeysuckle
/plants/flame-honeysuckle.description: Attracts butterflies and hummingbirds. Also try A. thurberi. Photo credit: Greg Corman.

/plants/flattop-buckwheat.name: Flattop Buckwheat
/plants/flattop-buckwheat.description: Suited to small spaces. Tiny flowers and seeds attract bees, birds, and butterflies.

/plants/floss-silk-tree.name: Floss Silk Tree
/plants/floss-silk-tree.description: Distinctive trunk and puts on a spectacular show of flowers in the fall. Look for selections that offer a variety of flower colors. Previously classified as Chorisia speciosa.

/plants/foothills-palo-verde.name: Foothills Palo Verde
/plants/foothills-palo-verde.description: Good for naturalistic landscapes. Provides seed and cover to birds and other wildlife. Previously classified as Cercidium microphyllum.

/plants/fourwing-saltbush.name: Fourwing Saltbush
/plants/fourwing-saltbush.description: Tolerates tough conditions and serves as an excellent wildlife plant. Photo credit: Kirti Mathura

/plants/garden-cosmos.name: Garden Cosmos
/plants/garden-cosmos.description: Attracts bees and butterflies with flowers in white, pink, purple, red, or magenta. Sow seeds in the spring or plant directly from containers. Photo credit: Kirti Mathura

/plants/giant-hesperaloe.name: Giant Hesperaloe
/plants/giant-hesperaloe.description: Unusual accent adds drama to the landscape. Stalk blooms attract bees, hummingbirds, and nocturnal pollinators.

/plants/globe-mallow.name: Globe Mallow
/plants/globe-mallow.description: Look for selections that offer a wide range of flower colors. Purchase this plant in bloom to select desired flower color.

/plants/golden-barrel.name: Golden Barrel
/plants/golden-barrel.description: A striking accent that is especially attractive in groupings.

/plants/golden-dyssodia.name: Golden Dyssodia
/plants/golden-dyssodia.description: Sow seeds in the fall or plant from containers. May be sold as Thymophylla pentachaeta.

/plants/golden-eye.name: Golden Eye
/plants/golden-eye.description: Good for naturalistic landscapes. Also try Viguiera stenoloba and Trixis californica. Previously classified as V. deltoidea.

/plants/gooddings-verbena.name: Goodding's Verbena
/plants/gooddings-verbena.description: Fragrant flowers attract butterflies. Sow seeds in the fall. Previously classified as Verbena gooddingii.

/plants/grape-ivy.name: Grape Ivy
/plants/grape-ivy.description: Allow to climb in trees or drape over retaining walls for an interesting effect.

/plants/grass-tree.name: Grass Tree
/plants/grass-tree.description: Exceptional specimen plant. May be sold as D. longissimum.

/plants/gray-thorn.name: Gray Thorn
/plants/gray-thorn.description: Provides shelter for wildlife. Blue-black fruits attract birds.

/plants/guajillo.name: Guajillo
/plants/guajillo.description: Lush-looking shrub for screening or as an attractive small tree, perfect for patios. Previously classified as Acacia berlandieri.

/plants/guayacn.name: Guayacán
/plants/guayacn.description: Provides a vivid flower color that attracts bees and butterflies. Seeds attract birds.

/plants/hildmanns-cereus.name: Hildmann's Cereus
/plants/hildmanns-cereus.description: A fast-growing substitute for organ pipe cactus. Also try Stetsonia coryne. May be sold as C. peruvianus.

/plants/hop-bush.name: Hop Bush
/plants/hop-bush.description: Decorative papery fruits attract birds. Can be used an alternative to oleander and effective screen.

/plants/hummingbird-trumpet.name: Hummingbird Trumpet
/plants/hummingbird-trumpet.description: Bright orange-red trumpet flowers attract hummingbirds. Previously classified as Zauschneria California.

/plants/hybrid-palo-verde.name: Hybrid Palo Verde
/plants/hybrid-palo-verde.description: May be short-lived and can be prone to storm damage. Overwatering may cause limbs to break. Previously classified as Cercidium hybrid.

/plants/indian-fig.name: Indian Fig
/plants/indian-fig.description: Mostly spineless with showy fruits and tree-like sculptural qualities.

/plants/jerusalem-sage.name: Jerusalem Sage
/plants/jerusalem-sage.description: Intense yellow flowers that bloom from spring to summer.

/plants/jojoba.name: Jojoba
/plants/jojoba.description: Good for naturalistic landscapes, screening, or as an informal hedge.

/plants/katie-ruellia.name: Katie Ruellia
/plants/katie-ruellia.description: Refined groundcover for small areas. Look for selections that offer pink or white flowers. May be sold as R. brittoniana 'Katie'.

/plants/kidneywood.name: Kidneywood
/plants/kidneywood.description: Grown as a shrub or small tree. Fragrant, white spike flowers. Good for a naturalistic setting and near patios. Photo credit: Kirti Mathura

/plants/langmans-sage.name: Langman's Sage
/plants/langmans-sage.description: Flowers in response to monsoon rains. Provides significant summer color. Also try L. pruinosum and L. zygophyllum.

/plants/lantana.name: Lantana
/plants/lantana.description: Long lasting, fragrant flowers provide vibrant summer color and attract butterflies. Look for selections that offer a variety of flower colors.

/plants/leatherleaf-acacia.name: Leatherleaf Acacia
/plants/leatherleaf-acacia.description: Good for small spaces or in large containers. Also try A. aneura.

/plants/lilac-vine.name: Lilac Vine
/plants/lilac-vine.description: Provides winter color. Requires well-drained soil.

/plants/little-leaf-ash.name: Little Leaf Ash
/plants/little-leaf-ash.description: Graceful shrub or a small tree. Features attractive gray bark with age.

/plants/little-leaf-cordia.name: Little Leaf Cordia
/plants/little-leaf-cordia.description: Produces bright white flower clusters from spring to fall and is an effective screen or informal hedge.

/plants/live-oak.name: Live Oak
/plants/live-oak.description: Accepts lawn conditions. Consider mature size when selecting plant location.

/plants/mangle-dulce.name: Mangle Dulce
/plants/mangle-dulce.description: Highly salt tolerant. Does well in containers.

/plants/mastic-tree.name: Mastic Tree
/plants/mastic-tree.description: Can be used for screening or trained into a small specimen tree.

/plants/maximilian-sunflower.name: Maximilian Sunflower
/plants/maximilian-sunflower.description: Birds love to eat the seeds. Sow seeds in spring for fall blooms. Photo credit: Kirti Mathura

/plants/mealy-cup-sage.name: Mealy Cup Sage
/plants/mealy-cup-sage.description: Blue-purple flowers attract bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds.

/plants/medicinal-aloe.name: Medicinal Aloe
/plants/medicinal-aloe.description: Prolific and tough. May be sold as A. barbadensis.

/plants/mescal-ceniza.name: Mescal Ceniza
/plants/mescal-ceniza.description: Striking banded leaves with distinctive toothed margins. Also try A. chrysantha, A. murpheyi, and A. palmeri.

/plants/mexican-bird-of-paradise.name: Mexican Bird of Paradise
/plants/mexican-bird-of-paradise.description: Intermittent yellow flower spikes throughout the year. Previously classified as Caesalpinia mexicana.

/plants/mexican-blue-palm.name: Mexican Blue Palm
/plants/mexican-blue-palm.description: Bold tropical palm that is well suited to containers and provides an \\

/plants/mexican-buckeye.name: Mexican Buckeye
/plants/mexican-buckeye.description: Can be grown into a large shrub or small patio tree. Features fragrant flowers.

/plants/mexican-bush-sage.name: Mexican Bush Sage
/plants/mexican-bush-sage.description: Velvety purple flowers attract bees and hummingbirds.

/plants/mexican-ebony.name: Mexican Ebony
/plants/mexican-ebony.description: Good for naturalistic landscapes. Previously classified as Pithecellobium mexicanum.

/plants/mexican-fencepost.name: Mexican Fencepost
/plants/mexican-fencepost.description: Can serve as a bold, dramatic accent in the landscape. Does well in containers. May be sold as Marginatocereus marginatus or Stenocereus marginatus.

/plants/mexican-gold-poppy.name: Mexican Gold Poppy
/plants/mexican-gold-poppy.description: Reseeds readily. Sow seeds in the fall.

/plants/moss-verbena.name: Moss Verbena
/plants/moss-verbena.description: Provides colorful cover for bare surfaces. Previously classified as Verbena tenera. Also try G. peruviana and Verbena rigida.

/plants/myoporum.name: Myoporum
/plants/myoporum.description: Provides good cover on slopes. May die if overwatered.

/plants/ocotillo.name: Ocotillo
/plants/ocotillo.description: Striking silhouette with red-orange flower clusters that attract carpenter bees and hummingbirds. Also try F. diguetti and F. macdougalii.

/plants/octopus-agave.name: Octopus Agave
/plants/octopus-agave.description: Attractive form with smooth margins and soft terminal thorns. Also try A. bracteosa.

/plants/oleander.name: Oleander
/plants/oleander.description: Excellent screen and provides good summer color. Look for selections that offer a variety of flower colors and plant sizes. All plant parts are poisonous. Dwarf sizing noted below. Standard varieties can grow to 20' tall or more.

/plants/orange-bells.name: Orange Bells
/plants/orange-bells.description: Can serve as a colorful background screen. Also try T. garrocha.

/plants/orange-zexmenia.name: Orange Zexmenia
/plants/orange-zexmenia.description: Previously classified as Zexmenia hispida and W. texana.

/plants/organ-pipe.name: Organ Pipe
/plants/organ-pipe.description: Provides for a striking focal point over time. Blooms at night and pollinated primarily by nectar-feeding bats.

/plants/owls-clover.name: Owl's Clover
/plants/owls-clover.description: Charming wildflower. Sow seeds in the early fall. Previously classified as Orthocarpus purpurascens.

/plants/paleleaf-yucca.name: Paleleaf Yucca
/plants/paleleaf-yucca.description: Good for small spaces and containers. Pollinated by yucca moths. Also try Y. glorious v. recurvifolia and Y. rupicola.

/plants/palo-blanco.name: Palo Blanco
/plants/palo-blanco.description: Striking white, peeling bark and fine textured foliage makes for a nice accent tree in landscapes. Previously classified as Acacia willardiana.

/plants/palo-brea.name: Palo Brea
/plants/palo-brea.description: Distinctive sculptural form with lime-green bark. Previously classified as Cercidium praecox.

/plants/paperflower.name: Paperflower
/plants/paperflower.description: Great summer color with flowers following monsoon rains.

/plants/parrys-agave.name: Parry's Agave
/plants/parrys-agave.description: Particularly decorative with distinctive leaf impressions. Also try A. macroacantha, A. neomexicana, and A. parryi v. truncata.

/plants/parrys-penstemon.name: Parry's Penstemon
/plants/parrys-penstemon.description: Plant in the fall for spring flowers. Reseeds readily. Also try P. palmeri.

/plants/partridge-breast-aloe.name: Partridge Breast Aloe
/plants/partridge-breast-aloe.description: Great option for small spaces, narrow areas, and containers. Also try hybrid A. x 'Blue Elf' and A. striata.

/plants/pink-fairy-duster.name: Pink Fairy Duster
/plants/pink-fairy-duster.description: Pink flowers attract butterflies and hummingbirds.

/plants/pink-muhly.name: Pink Muhly
/plants/pink-muhly.description: For added effect, locate where flower plumes will be backlit by the sun. Look for selections with deep pink color.

/plants/pink-trumpet-vine.name: Pink Trumpet Vine
/plants/pink-trumpet-vine.description: Features lightly fragrant flowers. Occasionally confused with the Pandorea species.

/plants/pomegranate.name: Pomegranate
/plants/pomegranate.description: Fruit is colorful and edible. Foliage turns yellow in fall before dropping. Pollinated by bees. Look for selections that offer a variety of flower colors, fruit characteristics, and plant sizes.

/plants/prairie-zinnia.name: Prairie Zinnia
/plants/prairie-zinnia.description: Provides summer color and attracts butterflies.

/plants/purple-prickly-pear.name: Purple Prickly Pear
/plants/purple-prickly-pear.description: Cold or dry weather causes pads to take on striking purplish color. Also try O. macrocentra.

/plants/purple-ruellia.name: Purple Ruellia
/plants/purple-ruellia.description: Attracts bees and butterflies. Spreads easily with ample water and no containment. Previously classified as R. brittoniana.

/plants/queens-wreath.name: Queen's Wreath
/plants/queens-wreath.description: Good for hot areas. Dies back with cold, regrows in spring. Look for selections with red or white flowers.

/plants/rain-lily.name: Rain Lily
/plants/rain-lily.description: Flowers often appear after summer rains. Also try Z. grandiflora for pink flowers, Z. citrina for yellow flowers, and hybrids.

/plants/red-bird-of-paradise.name: Red Bird of Paradise
/plants/red-bird-of-paradise.description: Provides showy summer color. Look for selections with yellow flowers.

/plants/red-eremophila.name: Red Eremophila
/plants/red-eremophila.description: Provides late winter to spring seasonal color. Look for selections that offer a variety of leaf forms and flower colors.

/plants/red-justicia.name: Red Justicia
/plants/red-justicia.description: Bright red tubular flowers provide winter color. Good in containers. May be sold as J. ovata. Also try J. spicigera.

/plants/red-yucca.name: Red Yucca
/plants/red-yucca.description: Tolerates tough conditions. Look for selections with yellow flowers.

/plants/rock-penstemon.name: Rock Penstemon
/plants/rock-penstemon.description: Cherry red flowers attract bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds.

/plants/sago-palm.name: Sago Palm
/plants/sago-palm.description: Dark green pointed leaflets and a palm-like form provide an \\

/plants/saguaro.name: Saguaro
/plants/saguaro.description: Striking white blossoms serve as the state flower of Arizona. Flowers attract nocturnal pollinators, red fruits are enjoyed by birds. Shelters cavity-nesters. Consider mature size when deciding where to plant.

/plants/san-marcos-hibiscus.name: San Marcos Hibiscus
/plants/san-marcos-hibiscus.description: Showy flowers and glossy, heart-shaped leaves.

/plants/senita.name: Senita
/plants/senita.description: Flowers bloom at night on the \\

/plants/shirley-poppy.name: Shirley Poppy
/plants/shirley-poppy.description: Provides vibrant flower colors. Sow seeds in the fall or plant from containers.

/plants/shoestring-acacia.name: Shoestring Acacia
/plants/shoestring-acacia.description: Can serve as a tall screening tree with interesting leaves. Avoid overwatering.

/plants/shrubby-senna.name: Shrubby Senna
/plants/shrubby-senna.description: Fragrant flowers. Provides summer color. Also try S. polyantha (Cassia goldmannii). Photo Credit: Kirti Mathura

/plants/sideoats-grama.name: Sideoats Grama
/plants/sideoats-grama.description: Interesting seed stalks are relished by birds. Also try Aristida purpurea, especially for naturalistic landscapes.

/plants/slipper-flower.name: Slipper Flower
/plants/slipper-flower.description: Unique flowers and overall form. Does well in containers. Sap may irritate skin. Previously classified as Pedilanthus macrocarpus.

/plants/smooth-agave.name: Smooth Agave
/plants/smooth-agave.description: Attractive form with smooth leaf margins. Also try A. desmettiana 'Variegata' and A. angustifolia.

/plants/soaptree-yucca.name: Soaptree Yucca
/plants/soaptree-yucca.description: Pollinated by yucca moths. Leave dead leaves on trunk to avoid sunburn damage. Also try Y. faxoniana and Y. treculeana.

/plants/south-american-mesquite-hybrid.name: South American Mesquite Hybrid
/plants/south-american-mesquite-hybrid.description: Flowers attract native bees and other pollinators. Provides seed and shelter to birds and wildlife. Limit water to control rapid growth and possible windstorm uprooting. Look for thornless selections at your local nursery. May be sold as P. chilensis, P. alba, or P. hybrid.

/plants/spreading-fleabane.name: Spreading Fleabane
/plants/spreading-fleabane.description: Low-growing annual that attracts butterflies. Sow seeds in the fall.

/plants/spruce-cones.name: Spruce Cones
/plants/spruce-cones.description: Good container plant. Spineless with great sculptural qualities.

/plants/sugar-bush.name: Sugar Bush
/plants/sugar-bush.description: Can serve as an attractive screen or informal hedge. Fruits attract birds. Also try R. virens.

/plants/superstition-mallow.name: Superstition Mallow
/plants/superstition-mallow.description: Provides a subtropical effect and features heart-shaped, velvety leaves.

/plants/sweet-acacia.name: Sweet Acacia
/plants/sweet-acacia.description: Features sweet-scented flowers that attract bees. Provides food and shelter for birds and other wildlife. Previously classified as Acacia farnesiana. May be sold as A. smallii or A. minuta. Also try V. schaffneri.

/plants/tenaza.name: Tenaza
/plants/tenaza.description: Attractive bark and fragrant flowers. Previously classified as Pithecellobium pallens.

/plants/texas-ebony.name: Texas Ebony
/plants/texas-ebony.description: Foliage is a rich green color. Bark will sunburn if it is overpruned. Previously classified as Pithecellobium flexicaule.

/plants/texas-honey-mesquite.name: Texas Honey Mesquite
/plants/texas-honey-mesquite.description: Provides graceful character to the landscape. Look for thornless selections, where available. Flowers attract native bees and other pollinators. Provides seed and shelter to birds and wildlife. Allergenic (often caused by foliage). P. glandulosa v. torreyana is the Western Honey Mesquite.

/plants/texas-mountain-laurel.name: Texas Mountain Laurel
/plants/texas-mountain-laurel.description: Features fragrant, purple flower clusters, and velvet tan-gray seed pods in the spring. Seeds are poisonous. Previously classified as Sophora secundiflora.

/plants/texas-olive.name: Texas Olive
/plants/texas-olive.description: Can be grown as a shrub or small patio tree.

/plants/texas-sage.name: Texas Sage
/plants/texas-sage.description: Flowers in response to monsoon rains. Good as an informal hedge. Look for the 'Cloud' series, which offers a variety of flower and foliage colors.

/plants/totem-pole.name: Totem Pole
/plants/totem-pole.description: Particularly interesting for its unique sculptural quality. No spines. May be sold as Lophocereus schottii f. monstrosus.

/plants/trailing-acacia.name: Trailing Acacia
/plants/trailing-acacia.description: Good for bank stabilization and erosion control. Look for the prostrate form, as upright forms can reach 4 to 5 feet high or more.

/plants/trailing-desert-broom.name: Trailing Desert Broom
/plants/trailing-desert-broom.description: Utilize male varieties only. Look for selections with uniform growth habit. Tolerates tough conditions.

/plants/trailing-gazania.name: Trailing Gazania
/plants/trailing-gazania.description: Brilliant flower color. May die out in the summer if overwatered.

/plants/trailing-indigo-bush.name: Trailing Indigo Bush
/plants/trailing-indigo-bush.description: Tolerates tough conditions. Good for bank stabilization and erosion control. Also try D. capitata.

/plants/trailing-rosemary.name: Trailing Rosemary
/plants/trailing-rosemary.description: Fragrant foliage. Pollinated by bees. Upright forms are available.

/plants/triangleleaf-bursage.name: Triangleleaf Bursage
/plants/triangleleaf-bursage.description: Highly drought tolerant and good for naturalistic landscapes. Also try A. dumosa.

/plants/tufted-evening-primrose.name: Tufted Evening Primrose
/plants/tufted-evening-primrose.description: Fragrant flowers open from dusk to early morning. Seeds eaten by birds. Night blooms attract hawk moths and other nocturnal pollinators.

/plants/turpentine-bush.name: Turpentine Bush
/plants/turpentine-bush.description: Fragrant foliage. Provides food and shelter for wildlife. May be sold as Haplopappus laricifolius.

/plants/twin-flowered-agave.name: Twin-flowered Agave
/plants/twin-flowered-agave.description: Symmetrical slender leaves with smooth margins. Also try A. ocahui and A. victoriae-reginae.

/plants/velvet-mesquite.name: Velvet Mesquite
/plants/velvet-mesquite.description: Flowers attract native bees and other pollinators. Provides seed and shelter to birds and other wildlife. May be sold as P. juliflora. Also try P. pubescens.

/plants/violet-silverleaf.name: Violet Silverleaf
/plants/violet-silverleaf.description: Flowers in response to monsoon rains. Silvery leaves contrast well with green-foliaged plants. Look for the 'Cloud' series, which offers a variety of plant sizes. Not tolerant of poorly draining soils.

/plants/webers-agave.name: Weber's Agave
/plants/webers-agave.description: Bold specimen plant with smooth margins and sharp tips. Also try A. americana 'Mediopicta' and A. salmiana.

/plants/weeping-dalea.name: Weeping Dalea
/plants/weeping-dalea.description: Attracts bees and butterflies. Like most other Daleas, requires well-drained soil to thrive. Also try D. bicolor v. argyraea.

/plants/white-plumbago.name: White Plumbago
/plants/white-plumbago.description: Foliage turns an attractive maroon color in winter. Attracts and hosts butterflies. May be sold as P. scandens.

/plants/whitethorn-acacia.name: Whitethorn Acacia
/plants/whitethorn-acacia.description: Good for naturalistic landscapes. Flowers attract bees. Seeds attract birds and other wildlife. Previously classified as Acacia constricta. Also try Senegalia greggii.

/plants/willow-acacia.name: Willow Acacia
/plants/willow-acacia.description: Suitable screen for narrow areas and has fragrant flowers. Can reseed easily.

/plants/wolfberry.name: Wolfberry
/plants/wolfberry.description: Excellent wildlife plant. Provides shelter and fruits attract birds. Also try L. exsertum.

/plants/yellow-bird-of-paradise.name: Yellow Bird of Paradise
/plants/yellow-bird-of-paradise.description: Exotic flowers that attract butterflies and hummingbirds. Previously classified as Caesalpinia gilliesii.

/plants/yellow-bulbine.name: Yellow Bulbine
/plants/yellow-bulbine.description: Does well in containers. Look for selections with orange flowers.

/plants/yellow-dot.name: Yellow Dot
/plants/yellow-dot.description: Good in containers. Can be invasive if not controlled. Plant parts may irritate skin. Previously classified as Wedelia trilobata.

/plants/yellow-orchid-vine.name: Yellow Orchid Vine
/plants/yellow-orchid-vine.description: Yellow flowers are followed by large, paper-like pods that change color from chartreuse to copper when mature. Also try Mascagnia lilacina for purple flowers. Previously classified as M. macroptera.

/plants/yuca-vine.name: Yuca Vine
/plants/yuca-vine.description: Provides summer color. Dies back with winter cold but regrows in the spring.
